name: NIST Circuit Complexity AES tables: a smaller or shallower {AND, XOR, XNOR} circuit for the AES S-box, inverse S-box, MixColumns or InvMixColumns
compute_profile: laptop-days for the search (SAT and heuristic linear-layer optimisation, basis enumeration); verification takes seconds
statement: NIST's circuit-complexity team maintains straight-line circuits for the AES S-box, inverse S-box, MixColumns and InvMixColumns. The permitted gate model uses two-input AND, XOR and XNOR, with no constants. The supplied checked repository table lists minimum AND count 28 for each S-box direction, total gate counts 110 and 112, and MixColumns with 88 XOR gates at depth 5. These are construction bounds, not optimality results. Contributors are credited in the linked repository tables. The supplied page could not retrieve the NIST web targets; their applicability must be confirmed before claiming. The target is a circuit meeting a stated size/depth condition and beating all comparable published circuits and compositions.
success_criterion: Success means a circuit, given as a list of 2-input gates of types AND, XOR and XNOR only (NIST Circuit File Format or one 'GATE out in1 in2' line per gate), with no other gate types and no constants, that computes exactly FIPS 197 SBox(), InvSBox(), MixColumns() or InvMixColumns() under the NIST files' bit conventions (U0 and S0 are the most significant bits of the S-box input and output byte; for [inv]mixcols x_(8b+r) and y_(8b+r) are bit r, LSB = 0, of byte b), verified on all 256 inputs for [inv]SBox and as an exact GF(2)-linear map for [inv]MixColumns, and that meets at least one maintainer target listed on https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/circuit-complexity/list-of-circuits (direction: min in every case): (a) [inv]SBox with #AND <= 27; (b) [inv]SBox with #gates <= 105; (c) [inv]SBox with #gates <= 120 and gate depth <= 12; (d) MixColumns with #XOR <= 86; (e) MixColumns with #XOR <= 93 and gate depth 3; (f) InvMixColumns with #XOR <= 100 and gate depth <= 6. The selected metric must strictly improve the best comparable published circuit at verification time. For (a), compare AND count without limits on other resources. For (b), compare total gates without a depth limit. For (c), compare total gates among circuits with gate depth at most 12. For (d), compare XOR count without a depth limit. For (e), compare XOR count among circuits with depth at most 3. For (f), compare XOR count among circuits with depth at most 6. Check the live README, subfolder files, CSRC page and later publications. Recompute every comparison under the same gate model. The verifier recomputes all metrics: #gates counts every AND, XOR and XNOR; gate depth is the longest input-to-output path counted in gates; AND depth is the largest number of AND gates on any path. Include the best valid composition of published objects for the same parameters and metric in the bar, even if it is absent from a printed table. State whether the candidate is a composition. Identify its components and composition rule. Values in unmerged pull requests are not bars.

partial_wins.statement: An [inv]SBox circuit with fewer total gates than the live minimum for that direction (110 for SBox and 112 for InvSBox on 2026-10-14), at any #AND and any depth, verified as in the success criterion.

An [inv]SBox circuit whose #AND equals the live minimum (28 on 2026-10-14) and whose total gate count is strictly below the best listed circuit with that #AND (124 for SBox and 126 for InvSBox on 2026-10-14).

A MixColumns or InvMixColumns circuit with strictly fewer XOR gates than every listed circuit of the same function whose gate depth is at most the candidate's depth (on 2026-10-14 for example: MixColumns 87 at any depth, 89 at depth <= 4 or 96 at depth 3; InvMixColumns 90 at any depth or 106 at depth <= 6).
An [inv]SBox circuit with gate depth strictly below the live minimum for that direction (11 for SBox and 13 for InvSBox on 2026-10-14) at any size, or with AND depth 3 and at most 34 AND gates.

verification_method: Parse the gate list; reject any gate type other than AND, XOR and XNOR, any wire used before it is defined or defined twice, and any constant. Evaluate the gates in order. [inv]SBox: compare all 256 inputs with the FIPS 197 tables, most significant bit first (checked on 2026-10-14: this convention reproduces the listed aes-sbox-a32-ad5-g110-gd22-xx78-3 circuit on all 256 inputs, and x_(8b+r) = bit r of byte b reproduces aes-mixcols-xor88-depth5 as MixColumns). [inv]MixColumns: require XOR gates only, feed the 32 unit vectors and compare the resulting 32x32 GF(2) matrix with the byte matrices [02 03 01 01; 01 02 03 01; 01 01 02 03; 03 01 01 02] and [0e 0b 0d 09; 09 0e 0b 0d; 0d 09 0e 0b; 0b 0d 09 0e] in the files' bit convention (calibrate on a listed file first). Compute #AND, #gates, gate depth and AND depth in one pass, then compare with the live README tables, the subfolder listings (file names encode A, AD, G, GD) and the CSRC page, all re-fetched just before claiming. Seconds on any machine. Condition the comparison bar on the selected target depth or AND budget. For partial p2 compare total gates at the best AND count; for p3 compare XOR counts at depth no greater than the candidate. For p4 compare minimum gate depth without a size limit, or AND count at AND depth at most 3 for its second route. Recompute comparison compositions using the same checker and resource metric.
status_checked: 2026-10-14; historical source check from supplied batch A material. Current sources were not re-fetched during preparation.
angles: Treat the listed circuits as data: several 2026 entries were 'derived therefrom via linear optimization' of contributed circuits. Re-optimise the top and bottom linear layers of each listed S-box with exact or randomised linear-circuit methods (Boyar-Peralta exploring all ties, RNBP, Maximov-Ekdahl depth-bounded search, SAT-based exact SLP for small blocks) while keeping the nonlinear core fixed.

Enumerate tower-field and basis choices (polynomial or normal bases for GF(2^2), GF(2^4) and GF(2^8), and the isomorphism matrices) as Canright and Boyar-Peralta did, now with modern SAT/MaxSAT optimisation of each linear layer; the best basis for G need not be the best for A or GD.

For A <= 27, study how the A28 circuits beat the classical split of 32 ANDs (three GF(2^4) multiplications at 9 ANDs each plus a 5-AND GF(2^4) inversion), and search for shared bilinear products across the multiplications with multiplicative-complexity tools for 4- to 6-bit functions.

MixColumns is a byte-circulant matrix: impose its 4-fold rotation symmetry to shrink an exact bounded-depth SAT search (depth 3 is the natural first target), then break the symmetry. For InvMixColumns, seed from the factorisation of InvMixColumns as MixColumns times a sparse matrix.
Run many diversified searches in parallel and keep one Pareto archive over (A, AD, G, GD); improvements in one coordinate often appear as by-products of searching another.
pitfalls: The repository had 13 commits between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-08. Re-fetch the README, the subfolder listings and the commit log immediately before claiming. The CSRC page lags the GitHub README (it still shows InvMixColumns 113 at depth 6 while the README shows 107).
Gate set: NOT, NAND, NOR, OR, MUX and constant inputs are not allowed. Maximov-Ekdahl's 102-gate S-box and Canright's 120-gate S-box use other gates and are not comparable.

Bit order: U0/S0 are the most significant bits for the S-boxes, and MixColumns uses x_(8b+r) = bit r of byte b. A circuit correct under another convention computes a different function until its wires are permuted, and the claim must be about the circuit as submitted.

The README tables show selected circuits only: the subfolders hold more files (for example two A28/G131 S-boxes with gate depths 32 and 36, and the originally contributed A35/AD3 files), and the InvMixColumns folder holds 29 files against 8 README rows. Compare against every file and the CSRC page, and recompute metrics yourself rather than trusting file names.
Change-of-basis layers count: a tower-field S-box must take and return standard AES bytes.

Novelty: AI-assisted search is active on this exact table (the NIST team and outside contributors), so the window is short; also check ePrint and arXiv for 2026 AES circuit papers. The maintainers prefer wish-list targets to 'easy' small increments, so a partial win may beat the table without being listed by them.
